<reason>B justified reduced workload through existing evidence and focused comparisons while retaining fuller assessment for unresolved hazards. A never established why comparable screening becomes inadequate solely because the administrative pathway is distinct. B also answered the pressure questions directly, acknowledged farmers’ trade risks, and distinguished identifying editing history from tracing registered products. A raised legitimate concerns about regulatory boundaries, but its categorical claims that streamlining necessarily sacrifices checks and undetectability makes recall impossible remained inadequately defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B dismantled A’s “rigorous review or fast approval” dilemma by distinguishing assessment of existing evidence from generating an entirely new dossier. A’s own risk-tier alternative depended on that distinction; calling one system “triage” and the other a “jurisdiction” did not establish a different safety outcome.</best_rebuttal>
